subject: Week 15: sleep-training decision point; lock bilingual exposure
bodyText:
This week
Mid-regression for many households — catnaps of 30–45 minutes and continued night wakings are the expected texture, not a setback. Motor this week: pushing up on extended arms, bearing weight on legs when held standing, and rolling for some (CDC checkpoint: 6 months). Cooing turns are lengthening into consonant-vowel combinations, laughing is arriving, and his preference for the two of you is sharpening.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] 30–45-minute catnaps and distractible, popping-off feeds — mid-regression baseline.
- [monitor] A pattern worse than that baseline — wakings every 30 minutes, total night sleep under 8 hours, or naps only in motion. Document and bring to the 4-month visit.
- [monitor] No spontaneous smiling or laughing yet — add it to the visit list.
- [call within 24h] Fever with poor feeding, or acute illness signs layered on the sleep disruption.
- [call now] Fever ≥102°F rectal, true lethargy (hard to rouse), or apnea or color change during sleep; blue lips or unresponsiveness — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Lock the bilingual supply line now if a second language is the plan — perceptual narrowing closes around 12 months, and live human interaction is the only exposure mode shown to preserve non-native phoneme discrimination (high evidence, the best-supported domain this year). Two routes: a bilingual nanny (agency search runs 4–8 weeks; roughly $6,000–16,000/yr premium over monolingual) or an immersion infant room — Star Bridge Mandarin Immersion in West Portal accepts from 3 months, with 3–12-month waitlists. Target 25–30% of waking hours in the second language; passive audio and video are a verified zero. Star Bridge Mandarin Immersion: https://www.starbridgemandarinimmersion.com/
- Write the sleep-training plan as a couple this week if you are starting at 4 months: graduated extinction carries the most evidence, unmodified extinction acts fastest, and 5-year follow-up data shows no measurable harm from behavioral methods. Commit to seven nights before judging results. AAP sleep guidance: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Arrange floor toys in a semicircle just out of reach during belly time — pivoting on the belly is the current motor frontier.
- Add one flap-lift book (Where Is Baby's Belly Button?) to the rotation — anticipating the lift drives fine-motor reaching.

Upcoming
- Day 112–126 (Aug 31–Sep 14, 2026): 4-month well visit — bring the sleep log, feeding log, and any milestone questions.
- Days 105–140 (Aug 24–Sep 28, 2026): regression peak window — whatever response you choose, evaluate at the one-week mark, not night to night.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses arm to swing at hanging toys
  AAP window: day 90-150
  What to look for: Pre-reaching swiping — not yet visually-guided grasp.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/swings-at-toys/complete

- Laughs out loud
  AAP window: day 90-180
  What to look for: Full belly laugh, not just a smile with sound. Often triggered by gentle physical play or peekaboo.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/laughs/complete

- Reaches to grab a toy he wants
  AAP window: day 90-180
  What to look for: Visually-guided reaching, eye-hand coordination.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/reaches-for-toy/complete

- Rolls from tummy to back
  AAP window: day 90-180
  What to look for: Usually appears first — back-to-tummy follows later. Once rolling begins, stop swaddling for sleep.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/rolls-tummy-to-back/complete

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete
